native_result.query: At what Socioeconomic levels is the advantage in completion rates for Black students more pronounced?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))
native_result.HypoB: The Black advantage in BA-completion rates is most pronounced at the highest socioeconomic levels: raw rates show the Black-vs-non-Black gap turning positive only in the top SES decile (6.10% vs 4.78%, +1.3 pp), and after adjusting for ASVAB ability, class percentile, sex, and family size, the Black gap is positive above the median SES and largest and statistically significant around the 75th–95th SES percentiles. At low-to-mid SES Black respondents show a completion disadvantage (most negative gaps in deciles 2-3 and 7), which ability adjustment largely explains; the high-SES advantage persists beyond preparation. Findings are sensitive to binning (no positive gap bin at quartile resolution) and rest on rare events (~28 Black completers overall, ~5 in the top decile), so the top-level crossover itself is not individually significant (Fisher p=0.59); the support for the hypothesis is the monotonic SES gradient across bins, not any single cell.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8,773 rows, no missingness; SES continuous standardized, no documented bands). 2) Binned SES into pooled deciles (primary), quartiles and quintiles (sensitivity). 3) Computed raw BA-completion rates for Black, White, Hispanic, and pooled non-Black per bin with 95% normal-approx CIs on the difference and per-decile Fisher exact tests. 4) Fit logistic regressions: (a) BA ~ Black x (SES + SES^2) continuous interaction, unadjusted and adjusted for standardized ASVAB composite, class percentile, sex, family size — chosen after a pooled Black x decile-dummy model exhibited complete separation (zero Black events in the bottom decile); (b) Firth penalized logistic per decile for bias-reduced bin-level gaps. 5) Compared raw and adjusted gap gradients side by side and located where the Black advantage is largest/positive. Scripts: analysis_nls_ses.py, analysis_nls_ses_models.py, firth_check.py; tables in outputs/.
